interest: Shows wartime Allied moves against Japanese banks in Brazil, from feared fund transfers to Brazil's planned liquidation of the bank.
overview: File on Yokohama Specie Bank's Brazil branches: a 1941 cross-reference on Japanese fund transfers via Banco do Brasil, and a 1942 despatch reporting Brazil won't protect the bank and plans its gradual liquidation.

people.name: J. Edgar Hoover
people.role: Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation, Department of Justice

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a Department of Justice communication regarding Japanese counter-measures in South America against the U.S. blockade of Japanese funds.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Hoover's 1941 letter flags Japanese counter-measures using Yokohama Specie Bank's dollar account at Banco do Brasil.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Department of Justice Letter on Japanese Counter-Measures in South America

subfiles.about: Diplomatic despatch reporting that the Brazilian government will not protect the Yokohama Specie Bank or its staff and plans to liquidate its branches in Brazil.
subfiles.from: John F. Simmons, Counselor of Embassy (for the Ambassador)
subfiles.summary: Simmons reports Brazil's Bank of Brazil says it won't protect Yokohama Specie Bank or its staff, and is drafting plans to gradually liquidate its Brazilian branches.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 7491 from John F. Simmons on Liquidation of Yokohama Specie Bank in Brazil
